title: Why the Dollar Comes First
summary: Treat the dollar as pricing, funding, invoicing and liquidity infrastructure before interpreting an asset move.
learningObjectives: Separate the dollar as a currency quote from the dollar as global financial infrastructure.
Identify the upstream regime before forming an asset-specific view.
Recognize when a local catalyst is overpowering the common macro backdrop.
commonMistakes: Starting with the asset headline before identifying the upstream dollar regime.

title: From Bretton Woods to Fiat Discipline
summary: Read modern monetary discipline through credibility, inflation, rates, funding and balance sheets rather than a single metal anchor.
learningObjectives: Distinguish the end of gold convertibility from the end of dollar centrality.
Identify the modern channels through which fiat systems face discipline.
Connect historical monetary structure to current rates and funding conditions.
commonMistakes: Treating fiat money as a system with no market or institutional constraints.

title: USD Is Not DXY
summary: Use DXY as a specific developed-market basket, then confirm it with broader dollar and funding evidence before drawing a regime conclusion.
learningObjectives: State what DXY measures and what it omits.
Compare a narrow basket move with broader trade-weighted dollar evidence.
Treat divergence between DXY and broad USD as information rather than noise.
commonMistakes: Calling every DXY move a complete change in the global dollar regime.

title: How the Dollar Moves Oil, Gold, Bitcoin, Gas, and FX
summary: Identify the active pricing, funding, opportunity-cost, risk-and-hedge, or flow channel before interpreting an asset response.
learningObjectives: Name the main transmission channels used by the framework.
Explain why the same dollar move can affect different assets differently.
Move from regime to channel before reaching an asset conclusion.
commonMistakes: Using the dollar as a universal minus sign across unrelated assets.

title: Oil Is Not a Dollar Trade Only
summary: Read inventories, balance, logistics, spare capacity and disruption risk before applying the dollar overlay to oil.
learningObjectives: Rank physical balance before currency translation in oil analysis.
Separate demand-led and supply-led oil moves.
Use the dollar as an amplifier or offset rather than an automatic cause.
commonMistakes: Starting an oil explanation with DXY while ignoring barrels, inventories and logistics.

title: Gold and the Dollar
summary: Read gold through real yields, dollar direction and confidence demand instead of a permanent inverse-DXY rule.
learningObjectives: Assess real-yield opportunity cost before using a currency explanation.
Recognize when confidence and hedge demand compete with rate pressure.
Record disagreement among the three filters rather than forcing a clean signal.
commonMistakes: Treating gold as a permanent mirror image of DXY.

title: Bitcoin and the Dollar
summary: Separate Bitcoin's long-run monetary thesis from its current liquidity, real-rate, access and risk-appetite channels.
learningObjectives: Distinguish the strategic monetary thesis from the current-week trading channel.
Assess the dollar hurdle rate and broader liquidity conditions.
Recognize when access or crypto-specific flows dominate the macro backdrop.
commonMistakes: Assuming the long-run thesis determines every short-run price move.

title: Gas / LNG and the Dollar
summary: Read gas from storage, weather, pipes, terminals, export capacity and regional spreads outward to the dollar layer.
learningObjectives: Explain why gas remains regional even as LNG connects markets.
Separate benchmark language from physical delivery constraints.
Apply the dollar through contracts, funding and trade only after the regional balance.
commonMistakes: Treating gas as oil with a different label or as one uniform global price.

title: FX, Carry, and Translation Risk
summary: Read the broad dollar backdrop before the bilateral pair, then separate rates, funding, carry and translation effects.
learningObjectives: Distinguish a broad-dollar move from a pair-specific repricing.
Identify the conditions that support or unwind carry.
Separate transaction, translation and economic exposure.
commonMistakes: Treating a bilateral currency move as a complete judgment about one country.

title: Reading Regimes: The Eleven-Year Record
summary: Use the historical record to examine regime classification, failure modes and limitations without converting the score into a return forecast.
learningObjectives: Read historical alignment as regime evidence rather than investment performance.
Identify supply shocks, pivots and asset-specific events as weak zones.
Separate the frozen book record from the evolving live methodology.
commonMistakes: Treating a historical classification statistic as proof of future returns.

title: The Weekly Operating Framework
summary: Turn the framework into a repeatable sequence: identify the driver, record the three dials, add asset-specific evidence, and compare without forecasting.
learningObjectives: Start with the driver rather than the loudest asset move.
Record dollar direction, real-rate pressure and liquidity stress in order.
Treat contradictions as information and delay the published comparison until after an independent reading.
commonMistakes: Opening too many screens and confusing movement with meaning.

title: Common Mistakes in Dollar and Cross-Asset Analysis
summary: Detect one-variable thinking, benchmark overreach and narrative-first explanations before they harden into conclusions.
learningObjectives: Separate a useful relationship from a permanent law.
Use divergence to challenge the initial explanation.
Identify when a benchmark is being used outside its proper domain.
commonMistakes: Turning a true relationship into a universal and immediate rule.

title: What to Watch from Here
summary: Convert the framework into a continuing habit by recording confirmation, challenge, invalidation and the next evidence to verify.
learningObjectives: State what would confirm or challenge the current reading.
Refresh dated evidence from primary sources.
Use the live site as a continuation of the book rather than a replacement for it.
commonMistakes: Treating a completed reading as permanent after the evidence changes.
